title: Lesson 51 - What an Agent Template Is, and How Template Promotion Differs from Agent Promotion
description: Identify the considerations for deploying a template from sandbox to production.

questions.question: A partner must ship an Agentforce agent to customer orgs as a package. What is the correct approach?
options: Create an agent template, include the template in the package, and create a new agent from that template in the target org
Package the agent record directly, since an agent is metadata
Export the agent's testing cases and import them into each target org
Deploy the agent user record inside the package so the agent runs immediately
questions.explanation: The agent itself cannot be packaged directly, so the template is the unit you include in the package and you instantiate an agent from it in the target org.

questions.question: After deploying a template to a target org, what still has to happen before the agent is usable there?
options: Nothing, because deploying the template deploys the agent with it
Retrieve the agent metadata a second time so the actions resolve
Create the agent from the template, name it, and select or create its agent user record
Convert the template back into a legacy Bot before it can run
questions.explanation: Promoting a template moves a blueprint, so the target org still creates the agent from the template and supplies the agent's identity and its user record.

questions.question: Which statement about the relationship between a template and an agent type is correct?
options: A template can belong to several agent types at once
A type can be associated with many templates, but a template is associated with exactly one type, so the target org must have that type
A template has no relationship to an agent type at all
Any template can create an agent from any type as long as metadata is enabled
questions.explanation: A template is a child of exactly one agent type, so creating an agent from it in the target org requires that type and its permissions to be present.
